text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Fate of "solidarity surcharge" on income tax uncertain after state premiers in eastern Germany speak out against planned cut in the levy.
- Investment incentives for eastern Germany to be cut back.
- Labour Minister Norbert Bleum accuses employers of not doing enough to create jobs.
- German workers took fewer days off because of illness last year.
HANDELSBLATT
- Finance Ministry state secretary Juergen Stark says there will be no European Union "economic government" of politicians running the planned single currency.
- Untility RWE plans to change its ownership structure, with the Westdeutsche Landesbank as a possible shareholder, Der Spiegel magazine reports.
- Battle among European cities for financial market supremacy begins.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Bosnian Serb war criminal could serve his sentence in a Bavarian jail.
- German electronics industry complains of lack of action to encourage Germany as an industrial location.
- Former head of Veba Immobilien detained by prosecutors.
DIE WELT
- One million people dance in centre of Berlin in city's annual Love Parade.
- Length of average hospital stay is shortening, survey shows.
- Parliamentary president Rita Suessmuth defends German political system in face of criticism from industry.
- Hospitals in crisis as economic pressure on them increases.
- Wolfgang Schaeuble, parliamentary leader of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats, says halving the unemployment total by year 2000 will not be possible.
